hyperframes.notes_for_integration:
- **Pipeline order:**
  1. `node generate-hf.mjs design.json rough.mp4 outDir`
  2. `npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.145 lint --json` and gate on `.ok` and `errorCount==0`.
  3. `check --json` and gate on `.ok`. It takes about 30 s because it launches Chrome. Skip it in production if time matters, since lint covers the structural rules.
  4. `render --quality looks -w auto -o out.mp4`, run in outDir.
- **No TTY:** `init` is not required; the generator writes the three scaffold files itself.
- **Duration:** root data-duration must be a literal in the HTML. The generator rounds up to a whole number of frames (597 frames = 19.9 s at 30 fps), and the output is exactly 19.900 s with 597 frames.
- **Audio:** comes from the <audio id> element. The AAC is effectively copied (160 dB apsnr against the source), so there is no audio re-encode loss.
- **Media copy:** the generator copies the mp4 into outDir/assets (8.6 MB). For production, consider a hardlink or rendering in place to avoid the copy.
- **Machine-readable progress:** `@hf-progress {...}` lines and `[INFO] [Render:trace] {json}` lines carry workerCount, captureMode and forceScreenshot. The last summary line is the stage line.
- **Cost on this PC:** about 54 s per 20 s reel, roughly 2.7x realtime, single worker, CPU encode streamed during capture. Disabling low-memory mode with 3 workers gives about 45 s.
- **Lint-clean caption pattern:** root-level `section.clip.caption-group[data-track-kind=captions]` with only span descendants. Centre by padding the full-frame clip, never with transform. Tween inner spans with fromTo and immediateRender:false for every tween except an element's first.
- **Fonts:** a local @font-face named "Inter" is embedded as a data URI by the compiler, and no Google Fonts fetch happens.
- **GSAP:** inlined from the CDN at compile time, so network is required unless you pass --gsap with a local file.
- **Upstream fix:** stage 3 should encode rough cuts with a 1 s GOP to clear the sparse-keyframe warning.
- **Text measurement:** the glyph-width estimates in the generator (font-size fit and pop cap) are heuristics. A sturdier version would measure with window.__hyperframes.pretext before building the timeline.
- **Artifacts in hf/:** index.html, assets/, lint.json, check.json, render.log, render.time.txt, out.ffprobe.txt, snap_1/9/18.png, plus renders/out_w3.mp4 and render_w3.log from the 3-worker experiment.
- **Constraints kept:** nothing under C:/Users/firda/монтаж/src was touched, and nothing was committed.

remotion.notes_for_integration:
To integrate into the pipeline:
- Install once per machine, not per job: one shared Remotion project with node_modules (731 MB including Chrome Headless Shell), then bundle() once per code version and reuse the serveUrl for every output.
- A job only needs (a) the rough mp4 and font reachable from public/ (or publicDir, or a local HTTP URL passed in props) and (b) inputProps = the design job.
- render.mjs already shows the shape: openBrowser() once, shared by selectComposition, renderStill and renderMedia. For several outputs, loop selectComposition and renderMedia over jobs with the same serveUrl and browser.
- Note that only public/ is copied at bundle time. Per-job videos therefore need either a copy into public/ before bundle(), a publicDir per batch, or a local static server URL in props. The prototype copies into public/.

Settings to keep:
- colorSpace:'bt709', so output is yuv420p, tv range, bt709. Also tag the rough cuts bt709 upstream.
- concurrency 2 on this 8 GB machine.
- crf 18, preset veryfast.

Measured on reel_1: about 35 s renderMedia plus about 2 s overhead per 20 s reel (17 fps).

The output still goes through the existing finalize step (two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS). Remotion's AAC is a re-encode at the same level as the source, so loudnorm should behave as before.

Licence (from the research doc): renderMedia from code counts as 'Remotion for Automators'. It is free for 3 or fewer people, otherwise $0.01/render with a $100/month minimum. v5 will require licenseKey and make telemetry mandatory for Automators.

To regenerate: `node workspace/_proto/remotion-gen/generate-remotion.mjs <design.json> <rough.mp4> <outDir>`. It rewrites src/, props.json and render.mjs, and leaves node_modules/ and out/ alone.

judge.rationale: Both prototypes rendered the same 19.9 s reel correctly with audio, so the choice is made on the margins. Quality is a tie at frame level and slightly favours HyperFrames at glyph level: its 8 px stroke (4 px visible under paint-order) keeps the counters of Р/В/О/Д open and the yellow word reads as a word, whereas Remotion draws 16 px (8 px visible) and the outline clogs counters and merges neighbouring letters into one black blob; Remotion's veryfast/JPEG path is also visibly softer in the zoomed crops. Speed looks like a Remotion win (37.1 s vs 53.9 s) until the settings are equalised: HF's 53.9 s was a forced single-worker low-memory run with x264 medium CRF 16; with 3 workers HF's capture phase was 35.0 s against Remotion's 34.6 s renderMedia, so the Chrome screenshot engine is the same speed on this Windows box (~17 fps) and the residual 8 s is non-streamed encode, npx start-up and medium-vs-veryfast, all of which the adapter controls. Licensing is the decisive tiebreak for a company that will exceed 3 people and render many times a day: HyperFrames is Apache-2.0 with no per-render fee, no licence key and telemetry that we switch off; Remotion in our usage is 'Remotion for Automators' ($0.01/render, $100/month minimum), and v5 adds a mandatory licenseKey, mandatory telemetry for Automators and counts contractors toward headcount, i.e. a recurring cost plus a compliance obligation baked into the render path. HyperFrames also fits SPEC §5.5 better: overlays are plain HTML+GSAP that an LLM with the locally installed hyperframes-* skills can author, and `lint`/`check` give us automated layout, contrast and caption-zone gates for generated compositions that we would otherwise have to build ourselves on Remotion. Remotion's genuinely better programmatic API (bundle once, shared browser, typed inputProps, onProgress, cancel) is real, but the HF equivalent is a ~2 s subprocess per render with parseable @hf-progress lines, and the OverlayRenderer interface already in src/design/renderer.ts isolates that. Decision: HyperFrames pinned at 0.8.145 as the production renderer, installed locally (not npx), GSAP and the font vendored so renders need no network; the Remotion prototype stays in the repo as a second OverlayRenderer behind a --renderer flag so the fallback is one flag away. Re-evaluate if two consecutive HF pin upgrades break lint or render, if production wall-clock stays above 2.5x realtime after the worker plan on a Linux box, or if HeyGen changes the licence.

quality.hyperframes: Legible and clean. Captions: Inter 800 uppercase, centred at y≈1385, 8 px -webkit-text-stroke with paint-order (4 px visible) plus soft shadow; readable on green fractal, white, grey, black and saturated blue (check: 18/18 contrast, 0 layout issues). Active word #FFD600 popped to ≤1.12 with a growth cap; highlight clearly visible on every snapshot. Glyph edges are crisp (CRF 16, medium) and counters stay open. Defects seen: inter-word gap is too tight once a word is popped: 'СПРАШИВАЮТ, В' (snap_1) and 'ЛЮБИТ СПЕШКИ,' (snap_18) are nearly touching and 'ДИВЗИРА, ЕГО' is tight; the highlighted trailing comma hangs into the next word; page 1 ends on the orphan 'В'. Title: rgba(0,0,0,.55) rounded box, sentence case, 88 px, no stroke, centred at y≈345, inside the 6 % safe margins and below the top UI band; correct but looks like a default template. No frozen/shifted frames (PSNR min 35.8 dB vs source), audio bit-identical (apsnr 160 dB), no visible artifacts, 19.900 s output for a 19.885 s timeline (one frozen tail frame).
quality.remotion: Legible, same layout, same colours and same title treatment (pixel-equivalent box). Differences at glyph scale: the outline is drawn at 2×stroke_width = 16 px so 8 px is visible, which makes the yellow word a heavy black sticker, clogs the counters of Р/В/О/Д and merges adjacent letters; edges are softer (crf 18 veryfast with the JPEG intermediate), visible in the zoomed 'ДИВЗИРА' crop. Word spacing was widened to 0.42 em to stop overlap, which fixes the pop collision but reads airy on short words ('ПЛОВ  НЕ' in snap_18). text-wrap: balance gives nicer two-line splits than HF's. Same orphan 'В' and highlighted-comma issues. Title identical to HF. Audio is re-encoded AAC (same level) rather than copied, so with finalize it is encoded twice; colour needed the explicit colorSpace:'bt709' workaround to avoid full-range bt470bg output. Preview PNG at 1.0 s matches snap_1.

speed.hyperframes: 53.88 s wall for the 19.9 s reel (2.7× realtime) with the machine-forced low-memory profile: 1 worker, screenshot capture, hardware GPU (ANGLE Intel UHD 770), x264 medium CRF 16 streamed during capture; stage line compile 0.6 · extract 0.0 (cache warm; 2.0 s cold) · audio 0.4 · probe 0.1 · setup 0.3 · capture 49.9 · assemble 0.4, i.e. ~12 fps capture. With --no-low-memory-mode -w 3: 45.07 s wall, capture 35.0 s (~17 fps) then a non-streamed encode of 5.8 s. First-run extras: +3.3 s (cold frame cache 2.0 s, first compile); the one-time npx package and chrome-headless-shell downloads were already cached and not measured. Per-render fixed overhead: npx resolution ~1.5–2 s plus compile 0.6 s. The capture rate at equal worker count matches Remotion's; the engine is the bottleneck on Windows (screenshot path; beginframe is Linux-only).
speed.remotion: 37.07 s wall (1.9× realtime), stable across three runs (36.3–36.9 s): bundle 1.1 s (warm webpack cache), openBrowser 0.1, selectComposition 0.2, renderStill 0.5, renderMedia 34.6 s for 597 frames = 17.2 fps at concurrency 2, x264 veryfast CRF 18, jpeg frames, encode overlapped. Concurrency above 2 was slower on this 2 GB-free machine (c4–c8: 7.6–10.8 fps) and OffthreadVideo at c8 hit a compositor error in the research run. One-time per machine ≈28.5 s: npm install 17 s (731 MB node_modules incl. browser), Chrome Headless Shell 125.9 MB download 7.5 s, first cold bundle +3.6 s. Not like-for-like with HF: medium CRF 16 vs veryfast CRF 18 (bitrate 7.3 vs 4.5 Mb/s) and streamed vs non-streamed encode explain most of the 8 s gap at equal worker count.

judge.licensing: HyperFrames: the hyperframes npm package (0.8.41 and 0.8.145) declares "license": "Apache-2.0"; the GitHub repo heygen-com/hyperframes is Apache-2.0 ("Copyright 2026 HeyGen, Inc.") and its README states no per-render fees or commercial-use thresholds. Caveats from the research doc: the tarball ships no LICENSE file (files: [bin, dist]) and @hyperframes/producer, core and engine publish without a license field, though they live in the same Apache-2.0 monorepo. Telemetry is anonymous and disabled with HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1. Keep the Apache notice; no warranty. Remotion: free only for "an individual; a for-profit organization with up to 3 employees; a non-profit; evaluating"; the threshold is headcount only ("as long as your total headcount is 3 or less"), no revenue test. Our Node pipeline calling renderMedia() per output is an "automation": "Remotion for Automators ... costs $0.01 per render, with a minimum spend of $100/month" once the company has 4 or more people; developers on automations need no Creators seat; no refunds; H.264/AAC patent fees not covered. Remotion 5.0 (not yet latest; npm latest is 4.0.534) ties the licence to updated terms, "Contractors now also count towards team size", requires a licenseKey in the rendering APIs ("free-license" if eligible) and makes telemetry mandatory for Automators. Remotion is source-available, not OSI open source. For a startup that will exceed 3 people and renders daily, HyperFrames has zero licence cost and no compliance hooks in the render path; Remotion is at least $100/month plus a licence-key/telemetry obligation and a headcount audit trail.
risks: HyperFrames is pre-1.0 (0.8.145) and moves fast: the prototype needed the undocumented caption-group / data-track-kind=captions exemption (CAPTION_CUE_TOKEN read from the lint source) to silence timeline_track_too_dense, and nested-structure rules changed between 0.8.41 and 0.8.145. Mitigation: pin 0.8.145 as a local devDependency, snapshot-test the generated index.html, run lint in CI on the fixture job, upgrade deliberately via `hyperframes upgrade --check`, and keep the Remotion adapter alive behind --renderer.

Low-memory mode is forced on any machine with total RAM ≤ 8192 MB (this dev box: 7859 MB) which pins 1 worker and skips calibration; --no-low-memory-mode -w 3 worked with 2.4 GB free but was never stressed. Production render boxes need ≥16 GB; the workers planner must derive worker count from free RAM (≈320 MB per Chrome worker) rather than trusting -w auto.

Windows is always the screenshot capture path (beginframe is Linux-only), capping capture at ~17 fps with 2–3 workers, i.e. ~2.3× realtime per output. SPEC §8's 5-minute budget for a 10-minute source with three 30 s reels is tight unless outputs render in parallel or the render stage runs on Linux (docker, beginframe). Remotion has the same Windows limitation (JPEG screenshots; shared-memory capture is Apple Silicon/Linux only).

Render-time network dependency: the compiler inlines GSAP from cdn.jsdelivr.net and fetches Google Fonts for any named family without a local @font-face. Mitigation: vendor gsap.min.js (vendor/gsap/, MIT) and ship Inter-Variable.ttf via a local @font-face (already proven to suppress the Google Fonts fetch); run with HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 and HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1.

The HF programmatic API (@hyperframes/producer: createRenderJob/executeRenderJob) is untested here and pulls full puppeteer with its own Chrome download; the CLI is bin-only. We integrate via child_process on the locally installed bin and parse @hf-progress / [Render:trace] lines; the summary path line is mojibake under PowerShell's code page, so never parse the human summary, only the structured lines.

Text layout in both prototypes is heuristic (0.7 em per uppercase char): HF gaps touch after the pop, Remotion gaps are too wide. Until widths are measured from the TTF at build time, long Cyrillic/Uzbek words can still collide or wrap unexpectedly on real transcripts.

Upstream rough cuts have sparse keyframes (8.33 s GOP; HF warned 'seek failures and frame freezing', no freezing observed) and are untagged for colour (browser assumes bt709, ffmpeg assumes bt601). The cut stage must write -g 30 -keyint_min 30 and bt709 tags or captions can drift onto frozen frames and colours can shift between tools.

HF pre-extracts every source frame (extract stage, 2.0 s per 20 s cold) into a frame cache; for many renders per day the cache grows and must be pruned, and it adds disk I/O per job. Keep it on a fast local disk and prune by age in the render orchestrator.

Duration rounding: data-duration must be a literal; 19.885 s becomes 597 frames = 19.900 s, leaving a frozen 15 ms tail. Finalize must trim to the rough cut's duration (-t) so A/V lengths match exactly.

Fallback cost: if HF has to be abandoned, Remotion brings $100/month minimum, a licence key and mandatory telemetry (v5), a 731 MB node_modules with a per-install Chrome, public/-coupling for media (copy per job or a local HTTP server) and the colorSpace:'bt709' workaround; the OverlayRenderer interface keeps that switch to one adapter but the design generator still has to be re-targeted.
Both renderers run captions in a Cyrillic path fine on this machine, but CI/docker images should keep workspace paths ASCII; the PowerShell summary mojibake shows how easily tooling trips on it.
judge.integration_plan:
## 0. Decisions that shape the code
- Production renderer: HyperFrames 0.8.145 as a local devDependency (`"hyperframes": "0.8.145"` in C:/Users/firda/монтаж/package.json), invoked as `node node_modules/hyperframes/bin/hyperframes.mjs`, never bare `npx`. Env for every call: HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1, HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1.
- Vendored runtime assets: `vendor/gsap/gsap.min.js` (3.14.2, MIT) and the existing `assets/fonts/Inter-Variable.ttf` + OFL. The composition references both by relative path so the compiler inlines them and no network is touched at render time.
- Overlays are rendered video-only (video `muted`, no `<audio>` element); the rough cut's AAC is muxed in at finalize. This removes HF's audio stage and the double AAC re-encode, and makes the overlay cacheable independently of loudness settings.
- Remotion stays as a second OverlayRenderer (`--renderer remotion`), not built or installed by default.

## 1. Module boundaries

### src/design (what to show, renderer-independent)
- `export.ts` (exists): keeps producing `DesignJob`. Add `frame: {width, height, fps}`, `duration` (ffprobe of the rough), `assets: {font_file, gsap_file}` as absolute paths, and `hold_gap` (0.6 s) so generators stop re-deriving them.
- `timeline.ts` (exists): `paginate` gains the function-word orphan rule and punctuation stripping (see design fixes); still pure, still unit-tested in tests/stage4-timeline.test.ts.
- `layout.ts` (new, pure): font metrics loaded once from the TTF (opentype.js, wght 800) → `measure(text)`; `wrapPage(words, maxWidthPx, maxLines)` with balanced two-line breaks; `popBudget(word)` = scale capped so growth ≤ 18 px/side; `wordGap(prev, next)` reserving only the measured pop growth; `holdWindows(pages, duration)` producing dispStart/dispEnd (hold ≤ hold_gap to the next page, else +0.3 s then exit). Output is a `Layout` object written to `layout.json`, consumed by every generator. This replaces the 0.7 em heuristics in both prototypes and is the single place a designer tunes spacing.
- `hyperframes/compose.ts` (new, pure: DesignJob + Layout → index.html string): standalone root `data-composition-id="main" data-width=1080 data-height=1920 data-duration=<literal> data-fps=30`; muted playsinline `<video id="a-roll">`; one root-level `<section class="clip cap caption-group" data-track-kind="captions">` per page with `<span class="cap-line">` per pre-wrapped line and `<span class="w">` per word; title `<section class="clip ttl">`; one paused GSAP timeline of explicit fromTo tweens (immediateRender:false after the first), registered last as `window.__timelines["main"]`; CSS generated from DesignSpec; vertical centring by padding, never transform. Moved and typed from workspace/_proto/hf-gen/generate-hf.mjs; snapshot-tested.
- `hyperframes/project.ts` (new, I/O): writes index.html, hyperframes.json, package.json, meta.json; hardlinks (copy fallback) rough_<id>.mp4, the font, OFL and gsap.min.js into `assets/`.
- `remotion/compose.ts` (fallback): emits only `props.json` for a fixed React project kept at `tools/remotion-overlay/` (the prototype's src/), bundled once per code hash; not part of the default install.
- `renderer.ts` (exists, extend): `prepare()` once per process (bin present, browser cached, vendored assets present); `build(job, projectDir)` returns `{entry, lint: {ok, errors, warnings}, notes}`; `render(projectDir, outFile, {quality, fps, workers, lowMemory, signal, onProgress})` returns `{file, seconds, stages, captureMode, workerCount, log}`.

### src/render (how to produce the file)
- `hyperframes.ts` (new): `HyperFramesRenderer implements OverlayRenderer`. build → `lint --json` and gate on `ok && errorCount === 0` (warnings go to the report). render → `render --quality <map> -w <n> [--no-low-memory-mode] -f 30 -o <out> --frames-cache-dir workspace/_cache/hf-frames`, cwd = projectDir, parses `@hf-progress {...}` into onProgress and `[Render:trace] {json}` into stages/captureMode/workerCount, kills the process tree on AbortSignal or timeout (duration × 6 + 60 s). `check --json` is exposed as `verify()` for CI and `vedit doctor`, never in the hot path (30 s).
- `remotion.ts` (fallback): the prototype's render.mjs as a class (bundle cache keyed by code hash, openBrowser shared, colorSpace bt709, concurrency from the planner).
- `workers.ts` (new): `planWorkers({freeMemMB, totalMemMB, cpus})` → `{workers: clamp(floor((free − 1024) / 320), 1, floor(cpus / 2)), lowMemory: workers <= 1}`. On this box → 3 workers + --no-low-memory-mode (measured 45 s vs 54 s); on a 32 GB box → 8–12.
- `cache.ts` (new): key = sha256(canonical DesignJob + layout.json + rough mp4 {size, mtime, head/tail 1 MB hash} + compose version + hyperframes version + quality + fps). If `design/<id>/render.key` matches and overlay_<id>.mp4 exists, skip build+render. This is also what makes `vedit revise` (SPEC §5.7) re-render only affected outputs.
- `index.ts` (exists, rework): per output: export → layout → build → lint gate → (cache check) → render → finalize. Stage overlap: design(N+1) runs while render(N) runs; finalize(N) runs while render(N+1) runs; whole outputs render in parallel only when the worker budget allows (total Chrome workers across outputs ≤ planWorkers). Report gains `capture_mode`, `workers`, `cache_hit`, `lint_warnings`, `stages`, `renderer_version`.
- `finalize.ts` (exists, change): `ffmpeg -i overlay.mp4 -i rough.mp4 -map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 -c:v copy -t <rough duration>` with the existing two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS on the rough's audio; preview JPEG as today.
- `cli.ts`: add `vedit design <job> [--only ids] [--no-translate]` (writes the project + lint.json, no render) and `vedit render <job> [--only ids] [--quality draft|looks|delivery] [--renderer hyperframes|remotion] [--workers N] [--no-cache] [--verify]`; `vedit run` chains cut → render.
- Upstream fix in `src/cut/index.ts`: encode rough cuts with `-g 30 -keyint_min 30 -sc_threshold 0 -colorspace bt709 -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -color_range tv`.

## 2. What the generator produces per output
`workspace/<job>/design/<id>/`:
- `design.json` — the DesignJob (timeline, pages, DesignSpec, media paths).
- `layout.json` — resolved lines, per-word widths, pop scales, gaps, hold windows (debuggable, diffable in revise).
- `index.html` — the standalone HF composition described above (one file, no sub-compositions).
- `assets/` — hardlinks: rough_<id>.mp4, Inter-Variable.ttf, OFL-Inter.txt, gsap.min.js.
- `hyperframes.json`, `package.json`, `meta.json` — scaffold equivalents written by project.ts (no `init`).
- after build: `lint.json`; after render: `overlay_<id>.mp4`, `render.log`, `render.key`, `stages.json`.
Final deliverables stay at `workspace/<job>/output_<id>.mp4` + `output_<id>_preview.jpg` + `render.json`.

## 3. How the pipeline calls the renderer
```
renderer = pickRenderer(opts.renderer)        // HyperFramesRenderer by default
await renderer.prepare()                       // once per process: bin, browser, vendored assets
plan = planWorkers(os)                         // workers / lowMemory
for output (pipelined, concurrency by RAM budget):
  job    = exportDesignJob(jobId, id, {translate})     // src/design/export.ts
  layout = buildLayout(job, metrics)                   // src/design/layout.ts
  key    = cacheKey(job, layout, rough, versions, quality)
  if cache.hit(key): overlay = cached
  else:
    built = renderer.build(job, layout, projectDir)    // compose + project + lint --json
    if !built.lint.ok: fail this output (others continue)
    overlay = renderer.render(projectDir, overlay_<id>.mp4, {quality, fps, ...plan, onProgress, signal})
    cache.store(key)
  fin = finalizeOutput(overlay, rough, output_<id>.mp4, {previewAt})
  report.outputs.push(...)
writeJson(render.json)
```
`vedit revise` reuses the same loop with `--only` = outputs whose DesignJob/layout/rough key changed.

## 4. Making renders faster
1. Workers from RAM, not `-w auto`: 3 workers + --no-low-memory-mode here (45 s vs 54 s); production boxes with ≥16 GB get 6–12 workers; each worker ≈ 256–320 MB.
2. Remove fixed overhead: local bin instead of npx (−1.5–2 s), vendored GSAP/font (no fetch), hardlinked media (no 8.6 MB copy), no audio stage (video-only overlay), frames cache on a local SSD and shared across re-renders of the same rough (−2 s), `check` only in CI.
3. Pipeline overlap: translation/LLM design, build/lint and finalize (ffmpeg loudnorm) all run concurrently with the next output's capture; capture is ~90 % of the wall time, so everything else is hidden behind it.
4. Parallel outputs under one RAM budget: a 3-output job on a 32 GB box runs three renders at 3–4 workers each instead of serially.
5. Quality presets mapped to HF aliases: `draft` → draft (ultrafast CRF 28) for revise loops and QA stills, `looks` → looks (medium CRF 16, default), `delivery` → delivery (slow CRF 15). Encoding is overlapped with capture, so presets buy ~5 s; the real lever is workers.
6. Linux render box (docker, HF `--docker`): beginframe capture replaces the Windows screenshot path; measure, expect a step change in fps. Plan the production render service on Linux from the start.
7. Cache by content key so unchanged outputs in `revise` and re-runs cost zero renders.
8. Measure continuously: `stages.json` per render and `render.json` wall_seconds feed a `vedit status` line; CI runs the fixture reel and fails if wall-clock regresses > 20 %.

## 5. Validation and rollout
- Unit: stage4-layout.test.ts (wrap, pop budget, hold windows, orphan rule, measured widths vs. the two prototype pages), stage4-compose.test.ts (index.html snapshot + `lint --json` ok), stage4-finalize.test.ts (mux + loudness + exact duration).
- E2E (CI, Linux): fixture job → `vedit render` → ffprobe (597 frames, 30/1, yuv420p bt709 tv, aac 48 kHz), apsnr of audio vs rough, PSNR of the uncaptioned band vs rough, `hyperframes check --json` with `--caption-zone` ok, contact sheet at 0.4/1.0/2.85/9.0/18.5 s stored as an artifact.
- Both prototypes succeeded, so there is no 'both failed' branch; if HF regresses at an upgrade, `--renderer remotion` is the immediate fallback (install tools/remotion-overlay, buy the Automators licence if headcount > 3).
design_fixes: Measure, do not guess: load Inter-Variable.ttf (wght 800) with opentype.js at build time and use real advance widths for line breaking, font fitting and the pop cap. Both prototypes used ~0.7 em per uppercase char and got the gaps wrong in opposite directions (HF touching, Remotion airy).

Word gap = 0.22 em base plus only the measured pop growth of the adjacent word (≤ 18 px per side, pop_scale stays the ceiling), so a popped word never touches its neighbour ('ЛЮБИТ СПЕШКИ,', 'СПРАШИВАЮТ, В' in HF snap_18/snap_1) and short words never float apart ('ПЛОВ  НЕ' in Remotion snap_18).

Strip trailing commas and periods from caption words (keep ? and !); the highlighted yellow comma in 'СПРАШИВАЮТ,' / 'ДИВЗИРА,' / 'СПЕШКИ,' hangs into the next word and reads as noise in uppercase pop captions.

Orphan rule in paginate/wrap: never end a page or line on a function word (в, и, не, на, с, к, у, о, от, до, а, но; Uzbek va, bilan, ham, uchun). Page 1 currently ends on 'В' and snap_18 breaks 'ПЛОВ НЕ / ЛЮБИТ СПЕШКИ' instead of 'ПЛОВ / НЕ ЛЮБИТ СПЕШКИ'. Decide balanced two-line breaks at build time and emit one <span class=cap-line> per line; never rely on browser wrapping.

Standardise the outline: stroke_width means visible width; draw at 2× with paint-order stroke fill; use 7 px visible at 72–84 px type (HF's 4 px visible is slightly thin on the busy fractal, Remotion's 8 px clogs Р/В/О/Д counters), and get the halo from a 0 3px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.55) shadow rather than a thicker stroke.

Safe areas: move captions.anchor_y from 0.72 to 0.68 and cap the caption/title line width at 0.80 W (≈864 px) so line 2 clears the TikTok/Reels bottom UI (y > ~1500) and the right icon rail (x > ~950); the title at 0.18 is fine (below the ~250 px top band) but gets the same width cap. Verify in CI with `hyperframes check --caption-zone`.

Page exit: hold ≤ 0.6 s gaps to the next page (keep), but a page that ends ≥ 0.6 s before the next one currently vanishes hard in HF (and holds 0.5 s in Remotion); hold 0.3 s then a 120 ms opacity/y fade on the inner span (never on the clip).

Pop motion: back.out(3) at 1.12 wobbles on long Cyrillic words; use back.out(1.7) at ≤ 1.10 with a 100 ms settle, and add the 'fill' word_animation (colour only) for calmer presets. Keep the last word lit through intra-page pauses (continuity), which both prototypes already do.

Title 'hero' treatment: drop the rgba(0,0,0,.55) rounded box (it reads as a stock template and the title has no stroke, so it depends entirely on the box). Use uppercase or title-case per preset, 96 px, the same stroke+shadow as captions, letter-spacing −0.01 em, line break after '—', and fit-to-width instead of a hard 2-line clamp; keep the box as a 'card' variant.

Data-driven backing: the understand/vision stage already samples frames; compute luma/variance under the caption zone per page and auto-enable a backing pill (rgba(0,0,0,.35), radius 16) when local contrast is low, instead of a global preset switch.

Exact timing: keep data-duration = ceil(frames) in the composition but trim the final file to the rough's duration in finalize (-t) so the 19.900 vs 19.885 s frozen tail frame disappears and A/V lengths match.

Uppercasing with the caption language (toLocaleUpperCase('ru' | 'uz')) so Uzbek Latin oʻ/gʻ forms uppercase correctly; never uppercase titles unless the preset says so (design.captions.uppercase covers captions only).

Upstream in cut: encode rough cuts with a 1 s GOP (-g 30 -keyint_min 30) and explicit bt709/tv tags; both renderers flagged sparse keyframes and untagged colour, which otherwise cause seek-freeze risk and colour shifts between browser and ffmpeg views.
